types.name: FWolangObjectLedger
types.doc:
One object's references from one owner (a vm, or the process when a callback
arrives outside any call the engine made). Several entries per address when an
object died and another was born where it lived while the script still held
the first one.

members.name: ReleaseAll
members.doc:
Every root still held, removed by slot: what a vm that is destroyed with
module-level vars still pointing at engine objects leaves behind. Answers
how many references were dropped.

members.name: Token
members.doc:
Tells two objects apart that lived at one address one after the other: the
slot's serial and index, asked only of an object Alive answered yes for. A
weak var remembers it when it is assigned, which closes the address-reuse
hole Alive alone cannot.

members.signature: static uint32_t PropertyOffset(const char* className, const char* key)

members.name: Remember
members.doc:
An object the engine is about to hand a script, recorded while it is
certainly alive so a weak var that ends up holding it is answered from its
slot. Objects a bound function returns are found by a scan on first use.

members.name: Orphans
members.doc:
Retains and releases that arrived on a thread running no engine call into
a vm (none should): counted here so nothing is lost.

members.name: SaveState
members.doc:
The object's `@Save` fields as the bytes `std.save` writes; false when the
instance is not playing. RestoreState replaces the object with one loaded
from such bytes (fields by name) and calls the script's `OnLoaded`, if it
has one; asked from inside a script call it waits for the next Tick, because
the object that is running cannot be swapped under itself. See WolangSaveGame.h.

fields it sends and writes the ones it receives through these. Both answer
false when the instance is not playing or the type has no accessor.

types.name: FWolangDiagnostic
types.doc:
One compiler diagnostic, read from the text the vm reports: what the
Message Log shows, with the file and line a click opens.

members.name: ParseDiagnostics
members.doc:
Splits a vm's rendered diagnostics ("error[E0026]: ..." then
" --> file:7:16") into entries.

members.name: ReportDiagnostics
members.doc:
The diagnostics of the last load or reload that reported any, and of the
last CheckProject; empty after one that compiled. The revision bumps on
every change, which is what the editor's Message Log page and status bar
item poll.

members.name: CheckProject
members.doc:
Compiles every script package of the project (and the engine classes'
shims) in a vm of its own and reports what it found; the editor runs it
when a script is saved and before Play. True when everything compiled.

members.name: IsAvailable
members.doc:
False on a platform the Wolang library is not vendored for; every script
actor then logs that once and does nothing.

members.name: HasEmbeddedPackages
members.doc:
Whether this module carries the engine's own package and Wolang's standard
library as data (loaded from memory, never from a folder); false when it was
built without the bindings.

members.name: GetScriptsDirectory
members.doc:
Where the project's script packages are: `<project>/Scripts`, or `<package root>/Scripts`
in a packaged game (which opens no project; `mbt package` copies the folder there).
Empty when there is neither.

members.name: FindPackage
members.doc:
A script path as an actor names it — project-relative or absolute, a
package folder or a .wo file inside one — to the folder holding its
wolang.toml; empty when there is none.

members.name: FindAny
members.doc:
Any world's vm, for calls that come with no world (a Visual Script
library node); null when no world runs scripts.

members.name: IsHotReloadEnabled
members.doc: wolang.HotReload: whether a playing world reloads a saved script.

members.name: GetCallBudget
members.doc: wolang.CallBudget: the ticks one call into a script may spend.

members.name: AdvanceTasks
members.signature: static void AdvanceTasks(const MWorld* world, double dt, uint64_t frame)
members.doc:
The world's script tasks (`task fun`, `wait Wait(seconds)`) advance by the
game's dt, once per frame however many script objects call this; a paused
world does not call it and slow motion passes a smaller dt.
